heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S handles Prusament PETG exceptionally well straight out of the box, achieving a reliable maximum print speed of 179 mm/s capped at a 15 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. No nozzle upgrades are required for this non-abrasive polymer, though keeping the top glass vented during long prints helps prevent heat creep in the enclosed chamber.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (clean with dish soap) or Smooth PEI Plate with liquid glue stick as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 15 mm³/s under Filament Settings > Advanced to ensure the print speed automatically limits around the 179 mm/s ceiling.
Lower Part Cooling Fan to Min 20% / Max 50% with fan threshold layer times between 10s and 30s to preserve layer adhesion and optical gloss.
Set Pressure Advance (PA) to approximately 0.038 s in OrcaSlicer Device Calibration to eliminate PETG blobbing at seam reversals on the direct drive extruder.
Enable 'Wipe while retracting' set to 1.5 mm and 'Retract on layer change' to minimize PETG filament stringing and nozzle buildup.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Severe fine hair stringing and web accumulation across travel moves
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG is hygroscopic and exhibits low melt viscosity at 248°C, which worsens when wet or without adequate wipe moves.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry filament at 65°C for 6 hours; set retraction to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s and enable OrcaSlicer 'Wipe while retracting' at 1.5 mm.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Excessive bed adhesion tearing PEI coating upon part removal
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PETG chemically welds to raw smooth PEI sheets at bed temperatures of 80°C and above.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Switch to a Bambu Textured PEI plate, or apply a thin layer of PVP glue stick or liquid release agent on smooth surfaces before printing.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle inter-layer bonding or easy layer separation under mechanical load
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive part cooling or excessive chamber auxiliary fan airflow freezing the extruded bead too rapidly.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Disable the auxiliary chamber fan completely and clamp maximum part cooling fan speed to 50% in the filament profile.

faq.question: Should I print Prusament PETG on the P1S with the front door open or closed?
faq.answer: Keep the front door cracked open or the top glass lid vented if ambient room temperature exceeds 25°C to avoid heat creep, though full enclosure is safe for smaller prints.

faq.question: Do I need to upgrade to a hardened steel nozzle to print Prusament PETG?
faq.answer: No, standard Prusament PETG is non-abrasive and prints reliably on the P1S stock stainless steel hotend without causing premature wear.

faq.question: Why is the maximum recommended speed capped at 179 mm/s?
faq.answer: At a standard 0.42 mm line width and 0.20 mm layer height, 179 mm/s consumes 15 mm³/s of filament, which is the realistic melt rate limit for the stock P1S hotend on PETG.

faq.question: Does Prusament PETG need to be dried before loading into the AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, PETG absorbs ambient moisture quickly, causing pops, stringing, and weak seams. Dry the spool at 65°C for 6 hours before placing it in the AMS with fresh desiccant.
